r18-001.gate_key: ind_polite | B1.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | I'd like to know why the meeting was moved?

key.correct: I'd like to know why the meeting was moved?
wrong: Could you tell me when the last bus leaves?
I wonder what she bought for her brother.
Do you know if Tom has finished the report?

item.why: *I'd like to know…* is not a question, so it ends with a full stop: *I'd like to know why the meeting was moved.* *Could you tell me…?* and *Do you know…?* are questions, so they keep the question mark.
item.why_lv: *I'd like to know*… nav jautājums, tāpēc beigās ir punkts: *I'd like to know why the meeting was moved.* *Could you tell me*…? un *Do you know*…? ir jautājumi, tāpēc tiem ir jautājuma zīme.
item.correct: I'd like to know why the meeting was moved?
wrong: Could you tell me when the last bus leaves?
I wonder what she bought for her brother.
Do you know if Tom has finished the report?

r18-003.gate_key: ind_polite | B1.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | I have no idea why my phone keeps switching off?

key.correct: I have no idea why my phone keeps switching off?
wrong: Could you tell me how long the course lasts?
I'm not sure whether I locked the front door.
Do you know who won the match last night?

item.why: *I have no idea…* is a statement, not a question, so it ends with a full stop: *I have no idea why my phone keeps switching off.* Only a sentence that asks (*Could you tell me…?*, *Do you know…?*) has a question mark.
item.why_lv: Teikums par *phone* nav jautājums, tāpēc beigās ir punkts: … *why my phone keeps switching off*. Jautājuma zīme ir vajadzīga, kad teikums jautā: *Could you tell me*…?, *Do you know*…?
item.correct: I have no idea why my phone keeps switching off?
wrong: Could you tell me how long the course lasts?
I'm not sure whether I locked the front door.
Do you know who won the match last night?

r18-005.gate_key: ind_advanced | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence means you give your manager an answer in either case? | Tell your manager whether you can work on Saturday.

key.correct: Tell your manager whether you can work on Saturday.
wrong: If you can work on Saturday, tell your manager.
If you can't work on Saturday, tell your manager.
Tell your manager that you can work on Saturday.

item.q: Which sentence means you give your manager an answer in either case?
item.why: *whether* = yes or no: you give your manager the answer in either case. *If* at the start is a condition: you tell your manager only in that one case. *that you can work* gives only one answer.
item.why_lv: *whether* nozīmē vai: vadītājam atbildi saki jebkurā gadījumā. *If* teikuma sākumā ir nosacījums (ja): saki to vienīgi tajā vienā gadījumā. *that you can work* dod vienu atbildi.
item.correct: Tell your manager whether you can work on Saturday.
wrong: If you can work on Saturday, tell your manager.
If you can't work on Saturday, tell your manager.
Tell your manager that you can work on Saturday.

r18-006.gate_key: ind_advanced | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence means you call the airline only when there is a problem? | If your bag doesn't arrive, call the airline.

key.correct: If your bag doesn't arrive, call the airline.
wrong: Call the airline to ask whether your bag has arrived.
Whether or not your bag arrives, call the airline.
Call the airline and ask if your bag has arrived.

item.q: Which sentence means you call the airline only when there is a problem?
item.why: *If* + a condition at the start: you call only in that case. *ask whether* and *ask if* report a question, so you call anyway to get the answer; *whether or not* = in both cases.
item.why_lv: *If* teikuma sākumā ir nosacījums (ja): zvanīt vajag vienīgi tad. *ask whether* un *ask if* nozīmē pajautāt, vai, tāpēc zvanīt vajag jebkurā gadījumā; *whether or not* nozīmē jebkurā gadījumā.
item.correct: If your bag doesn't arrive, call the airline.
wrong: Call the airline to ask whether your bag has arrived.
Whether or not your bag arrives, call the airline.
Call the airline and ask if your bag has arrived.

r18-007.gate_key: ind_advanced | B2.2 | mcq | Choose the correct option: ___ the delivery driver rings while I'm in the shower, could you open the door? | If

wrong: Whether
Whether or not

item.q: Choose the correct option: ___ the delivery driver rings while I'm in the shower, could you open the door?
item.why: You open the door only if the driver rings: a condition, so *if*. *Whether* alone cannot start a condition, and *whether or not* would mean you open the door even when nobody rings.
item.why_lv: Atvērt vajag vienīgi tad, ja kāds zvanīs pie durvīm: tas ir nosacījums, tāpēc *if* (ja). Ar *whether* vienu pašu nosacījumu nesāk, un *whether or not* nozīmētu, ka jāatver arī tad, ja pie durvīm nezvanīs.
wrong: Whether
Whether or not

r18-008.gate_key: ind_advanced | B2.2 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | Everything now depends on if the bank approves our loan.

key.correct: Everything now depends on if the bank approves our loan.
wrong: We haven't decided whether to rent a car in Crete.
If the train is delayed, I'll take a taxi.
Could you check whether the hotel has a lift?

item.why: After a preposition (*depends on*, *about*) use *whether*, not *if*: *depends on whether the bank approves our loan*.
item.why_lv: Aiz prievārda (*depends on, about*) lieto *whether*, nevis *if*: *depends on whether the bank approves our loan*.
item.correct: Everything now depends on if the bank approves our loan.
wrong: We haven't decided whether to rent a car in Crete.
If the train is delayed, I'll take a taxi.
Could you check whether the hotel has a lift?

r18-009.gate_key: ind_advanced | B2.2 | gap | The hotel wants to know ___ to expect us before ten, and ___ we're late, they'll keep the room for us until midnight. |

item.q: The hotel wants to know ___ to expect us before ten, and ___ we're late, they'll keep the room for us until midnight.
item.why: Before *to* + verb only *whether* is possible: *whether to expect us*. *if we're late* is a condition: they keep the room for us only in that case.
item.why_lv: Saka *whether to expect us*, nevis *if to expect us*. *if we're late* ir nosacījums (ja): viesnīca gaidīs vienīgi tad.

r18-010.gate_key: ind_advanced | B2.2 | gap | Complete with one word: The caterer needs to know ___ or not you're coming to the wedding. |

item.q: Complete with one word: The caterer needs to know ___ or not you're coming to the wedding.
item.why: Directly before *or not* only *whether* is possible: *whether or not you're coming*. *if or not* is a mistake.
item.why_lv: Tieši pirms *or not* var būt vienīgi *whether*: *whether or not you're coming*. *if or not* ir kļūda.
